text:
Matthew Schaefer is 19, the reigning Calder winner, and somehow better. He scored a hat trick against Columbus on Tuesday on nine shots, has a six-game point streak and 15 points in his last 10, and is playing 26:48 a night, two minutes more than as a rookie. That's 24 points in 20 games after 59 in 82 last season.

Our form check calls the run earned. His own chances are up to 0.67 expected goals per 60 from 0.49, and his recent shots carry more danger than his usual. Nine goals on 6.0 expected says the shooting will cool some, but the shape of his game doesn't need luck: he's in the top few percent of the league in skating speed and bursts over 20 mph, and last season Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 36% of his shots coming off the rush, twice the typical defenseman.

Evolving-Hockey had him driving play at the 99th percentile among defensemen last season while playing with weak teammates. For context, defensemen picked in the top three since 2005 have a median of 0.35 points a game in their first full season. He's at 1.20.
